clue.text: Excess 50 tons loaded onto ship that's wrecked

indicators.note: cargo loaded onto a vessel ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a wrecked vessel is broken up, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A cargo ship overloaded with fifty tons too many founders and is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations sit together inside the vessel before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilth is an old word for something spilled, hence a surplus or overflow beyond what is needed.

clue.text: You may need key to get at this gem

definitions.text: You may need key to get at this gem

parts.words: You may need key to get at this gem
parts.note: surface reading: a precious stone locked away in a safe or jewel box; setter's reading: the little key that rolled open an old tin of small oily fish, which is also the name of a gemstone

explanation.walkthrough: Old fish tins were opened with a winding key, and the same word is also a variant name for sard, a reddish gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small tinned fish and a gemstone, sardius or sard, as listed in Chambers.

clue.text: To murder a spy is devious, one only pretending to suffer for the cause

definitions.text: one only pretending to suffer for the cause

indicators.note: something devious takes a twisting course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: every letter of these four words

explanation.surface: Killing a spy under false pretences turns him into a fake hero of the cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means false, so a pseudomartyr is a sham martyr, feigning suffering for a belief.

clue.text: Taken to court? Praise in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Someone taken to court, then praised at the hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court hearing, which suits the definition, but it marks the sound-alike. The question mark flags a rare verb: to law is to go to law against.
explanation.definitionFit: To law someone is to sue them, so a person lawed has been taken to court.

clue.text: Manx figures embellished skirt essayist has on

indicators.note: embellished means dressed up and altered, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of skirt, rearranged
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer in a decorated skirt shows off Isle of Man emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia is a crossword staple for 'essayist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A triskelion, plural triskelia, is the three-legged symbol on the flag of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Composer replacing director with soprano displaying special gift

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: George Frideric Handel, the composer
D is the abbreviation for director; this letter goes out
S is the abbreviation for soprano; this letter comes in

explanation.surface: A composer swaps his director for a soprano and shows a special talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansel (or handsel) has nothing to do with the fairy tale here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansel is a gift for good luck, especially at a new year or a new venture.

clue.text: Directs Tree playing in opening of stage section

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the pair of opening letters
the opening of each of the two words stage and section is its first letter

parts.note: first letters of stage and section

indicators.note: the name Tree is played about with, its letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre note: the actor Tree is performing in the opening scene of one part of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Tree reads as the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree. 'Opening of' takes the first letters of stage and section, SS; 'playing' shuffles TREE to TEER, which goes 'in' that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or control a course, so steers is a verb synonym of directs.

clue.text: Exchanged (as once) page penned by hard-working student

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed as if in a pen, so it goes inside

parts.note: a swat (or swot) is a student who studies hard
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A diligent student swapped pages of notes with a classmate.
explanation.walkthrough: '(as once)' tells you the answer is an archaic form; swapt is an old past tense of swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapt is the obsolete spelling of swapped, meaning traded one thing for another.

clue.text: Upland country, wide and abandoned

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wide, an extra in cricket scoring
something abandoned is disused, old and left behind

explanation.surface: Open hill country that is broad and deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wold is a tract of open rolling upland, as in the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Shortly to bag a record, or something similar?

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a bag, so one piece goes within

parts.note: anon means soon, shortly
taken as written
a log is a record

explanation.surface: Someone about to grab a vinyl record, or something like it.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogon is an analogue, a thing corresponding to or resembling another.

clue.text: Line me up, excited about ascent for point closest to satellite

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the word for ascent
excited letters are stirred up, so the words line me up are rearranged

parts.note: a rise is an upward climb or ascent

explanation.surface: An instruction to a nervous recruit: get in line, excitedly, before going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' turns LINE ME UP into PELENIUM, split PE and LENIUM so that it goes 'about' RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Periselenium is the astronomical term for the point in a lunar orbit nearest the moon, our natural satellite.

clue.text: Plod retrogressively in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the word is used

parts.note: letters three to six of this word

explanation.surface: Plodding backwards in part of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrogressively' tempts you to read something backwards, but the answer sits forwards inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trog is a dialect verb meaning to trudge or walk wearily, which is to plod.

clue.text: Long-distance athlete creating damage on heart, running

indicators.note: running here means in motion, so the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: to mar is to damage
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner who overdoes the miles risks straining the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' sounds like part of the athlete's picture but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathoner competes in the marathon, the classic 26-mile road race.

clue.text: Graves? At least some are briefly occupied by Christian saint (7, two words)

indicators.note: a place occupied by someone has them inside it, so the saint's name goes within

parts.note: the abbreviated form of 'are' as in we're
Edwin, king of Northumbria, was the first Christian king there and is venerated as a saint

explanation.surface: Some graves have Christian saints buried in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graves' looks like burial plots, but it is the Bordeaux wine region; 'At least some' fairly qualifies it, since Graves is better known for white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux district whose wines include reds, so some Graves is an example of claret-type wine.

clue.text: Cigar that causes start of cancer of the mouth returning

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of cancer

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: oral means relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A grim health warning: cigars cause mouth cancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A claro is a light-coloured, mild cigar, from the Spanish for clear or light.

clue.text: Imprisonment? King fills debts with limits of sentence

indicators.note: whatever fills something sits inside it

parts.note: dues are sums owed
R for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of sentence

explanation.surface: A king jailed for unpaid debts serves out his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Duresse is an archaic spelling of duress, which in old law meant forcible restraint or imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress originally meant constraint by confinement, so the old form duresse can mean imprisonment.

clue.text: Pet, agitated, showing surge of energy, mental

parts.note: a cat is a pet
hectic means agitated, frantic

explanation.surface: An agitated pet suddenly has a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The term comes from psychoanalysis: cathexis is the investment of mental energy in an object or idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathectic relates to cathexis, the concentration of psychic or emotional energy on something.

clue.text: Giving youngster exercise, experience that involves manipulation

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: the craft that involves manipulation

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster
PE is physical education, school exercise
to try something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Making a child exercise is an experience in manipulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulation' sounds like controlling people, but it is working strings on figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the art of working puppets, which means manipulating them by strings, rods or hand.

clue.text: Unusual oak trees with hard inner framework

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their normal order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Some odd oak trees have unusually hard heartwood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests timber, but the definition describes sponges with a horny skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratose describes horny sponges, whose internal skeleton is made of tough fibrous keratin-like material.

clue.text: Talent? Genus has this for info

parts.note: the answer, split into two short words, is an instruction: applied to genus it removes the last two letters, leaving GEN, slang for info

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a biological genus can be called talented, as if a fact sheet were being written.
explanation.walkthrough: Easy to misread Genus as genius. Split the answer as NO US: apply that to GENUS and you are left with GEN, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical intelligence or common sense, a kind of natural aptitude or talent.

clue.text: Put on stone, getting old

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone gaining a stone in weight as the years go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suggests putting on weight, which fits stone nicely; it actually means presented a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a show is to stage it, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: What's-his-name in SA bagging duck as Aussie cheats

indicators.note: bagging something puts it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: dinges is South African slang for a thingummy or what's-his-name
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A South African bloke grabs a duck while Australians cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang to dingo is to behave in a cowardly or treacherous way, so dingoes here is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage, to dingo on someone is to betray or cheat them, named after the wild dog.

clue.text: Woman losing head about bit of part to run through

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
losing its head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of part

explanation.surface: An actress who loses her lead role is reduced to a bit part.
explanation.walkthrough: Empale is an old spelling of impale.
explanation.definitionFit: To empale is to pierce with a stake or spike, so it means to run through.

clue.text: Caddie found out recounting lots of old myths

indicators.note: out here means wrongly placed, so the letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A golf caddie caught telling tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddaic relates to the Eddas, the medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myths and legends.

clue.text: Mum on Sunday (but not always) cooked old-style chips?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, mum

indicators.note: cooked means the remaining letters are messed about with, rearranged
but not tells us to leave out the word for always

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Mother makes chips on Sundays, though not every Sunday, in the traditional way.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AY from SUNDAY leaves SUND, which 'cooked' rearranges to UNDS after MA. The chips are not fried potatoes but chip baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: A maund is a Shakespearean word for a basket, and a chip is a basket made of thin wood strips.

clue.text: Festival–original one–take day off

indicators.note: to take something off is to remove it from the whole

parts.note: the original holiday was a holy day, the first festival of the kind
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Taking a day off for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Holiday comes from holy day, so it is the 'original' festival; take away the day and the Hindu spring festival of colours is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Holi is the Hindu spring festival celebrated by throwing coloured powder.

clue.text: Billy etc end go on e.g. dodgems with one on board

parts.note: to cap is to top off or finish

indicators.note: someone on board is inside the vehicle, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: you ride the dodgems at a fair
a means one

explanation.surface: Billy and friends finish the day riding the dodgems at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy' looks like a person's name but is a billy goat, and Capridae is the goat family.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is an example member of the Capridae, the zoological family of goats.

clue.text: Stand sacks up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: A short instruction to stand the sacks upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a low seat or stand, as in a footstool.

clue.text: Transported prince in wretched thing, contraption partly stripped

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible creature

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
second, separate wordplay confirming the first: letters five to eight of this word, with its ends stripped

explanation.surface: A prince carried off inside some wretched contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wordplays lead to the same four letters: a prince inside a rat, and the middle of contraption with its ends stripped away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means carried away with delight, transported in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Mother with a son copies nanny

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.walkthrough: A nanny here is a nanny goat, not a child's nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Maa is the bleat of a goat, so to maa is to imitate a nanny goat's cry.

clue.text: Pipes cut all over the place with sound lagging

parts.note: a ding is a ringing sound

explanation.definitionFit: Ducting is a system of ducts, the tubes or channels that carry air or cables, so collectively pipes.

clue.text: Cooked tart containing hint of apricot fragrance

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: the opening letter of apricot

clue.text: Merchant? One such with onions includes me

taken as written

clue.text: Top of obelisk, pony dancing round right at centre of one

dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

amid means in the middle of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pony prancing round an obelisk in the middle of a ring.

clue.text: Old cattle fair: have a go with stall, getting rid of the lot

parts.note: to try is to have a go

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the lot means everything; these letters are removed

explanation.walkthrough: Tryst usually means a lovers' meeting; in Scots it was also a cattle market or fair.

clue.text: Scottish mounts? Pares down around start of climb

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece goes inside the other

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
